findings.reason: the plan should have listed `project_state.py` as a write path and folded `_cached_plan_state` onto `file_memo.file_signature`/`memoized`, the way `metadata_index.py:42` (post-plan) and `served_code.py:46` did, so a future signature-rule change has one owner.
findings.text: `_plan_file_signature` returns the same `(dev, ino, size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns)` tuple as `file_memo.file_signature` (`file_memo.py:30`), and `_cached_plan_state` (`:1191`) is a second hand-rolled stat-keyed plan-file cache beside `file_memo.memoized` (`file_memo.py:43`) with its own `_PLAN_STATE_CACHE`, its own lock and its own deeper-copy discipline; the plan's §2 write paths name `file_memo.py`, `serve.py`, `resources.py`, `roadmap.py`, `fleet_index.py` and `_plan_html.py` but not `project_state.py`, so the intended single owner did not absorb the pre-existing copy and two modules now key caches on the same tuple

findings.reason: these are pre-existing caches outside the plan's stated subject (discovery/rollup cost), and folding them in is follow-on cleanup, not a change to the discovery design this plan is about.
findings.text: `_PARSED_STREAMS` keys a cache on the same stat identity (with `st_mtime_ns` in place of `st_ctime_ns`) that `file_memo.file_signature` exists to own; alongside `ledger.py:744` and `capabilities.py:1181`, `grep -rln st_ino reckon/*.py` finds five modules holding stat-identity caches, of which only `metadata_index.py` was routed onto the new owner

findings.reason: a search that surfaced `_cached_plan_state` would have reached the same consolidation the `duplicate_owner` finding asks for at design time, before two owners shipped.
findings.text: the design's reuse map lists the call-sites it memoises and the walk it shares, but never records that a per-file, stat-keyed plan-state cache already existed in `project_state.py`; the negative-control section of §2 even measures parse counts through `_parse_meta_uncached`, showing the author reasoned about parses without surveying the caches already built to avoid them

findings.reason: this is the design's own stated principle (§7: "one entry point for every watch") applied to only three of the five derived views; naming the missing two in the design would change what §7 and §8b accumulate.
findings.text: one filesystem change must cause a reader to forget four things (the walk signature, the cached discovery, the metadata index rows and the parsed-plan-state), and the design exposes that as a call chain a maintainer must remember (`_invalidate_tree_views` calling `_invalidate_discovery_signatures` + `_invalidate_discovery_tree` + `metadata_index.invalidate_tree`, with `file_memo.clear` and the POST path outside it) instead of one module owning "everything derived from this tree, dropped together"; `file_memo.memoized` is the counter-example done right — an 87-line module hiding signature, deep-copy, LRU and torn-write safety behind three names

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the discovery freshness question ("is this result still current?") is answered by five separately-named entry points across two modules rather than by one owning module: `_invalidate_discovery_signatures` (`serve.py:1539`), `_invalidate_discovery_tree` (`:1644`), `_invalidate_tree_views` (`:1663`), `file_memo.clear` (`file_memo.py:83`) and `metadata_index.invalidate_tree` (`metadata_index.py:153`), plus a POST path that clears a sixth thing.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds `file_memo` as the owner of stat-identity-keyed per-file caching, but `reckon/project_state.py` keeps a second, independent implementation of the identical five-tuple signature and cache, and §2's declared write-path list omits `project_state.py`, so the new owner and the existing one fork.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the parse call-sites and tree-walk it extends (`_parse_meta_uncached`, `iter_resources`/`resolve_resource`, `_activity30`, `state-loader.js`) but proposes a new per-file memoisation module without citing the per-file plan-state cache that already existed beside it (`reckon/project_state.py:1180`, `:1191`, landed 2026-09-01 at `0ac65e732`, three weeks before `file_memo.py`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the layers the design adds (`resource_scan_scope` over `iter_resources`, `_FleetChangeWatch` over `_ProjectChangeWatch`, `_discovery_signature` over `_walk_discovery_signature`) each add behaviour the layer beneath does not have (bounded scan lifetime, process-lifetime multi-tree selection, TTL memo), rather than forwarding to it.
